Subject: Expedited close — cost crosswalk and batching/caching assumptions

Samuel / Alicia —

Putting a compact crosswalk on the MAP so we can unblock procurement and the final PO. Attached: HF_MAP_Costs_v3.xlsx (working tab) and a short assumptions PDF (MAP_Assumptions_v2.pdf). Key points we captured: tokenized pricing model at the Redwood hosted API tiers, candidate prefetch & KV-cache profiles, expected batching windows for typical HealthForge traffic (50–300 concurrent users).

Please confirm the following ASAP so we can land the MAP by EOW:
- Which endpoint profile do you plan to use (standard vs low-latency)?
- Rough steady-state QPS for inference calls (average and P95 burst).
- Any legal constraint on caching user prompt prefixes (we assume prefix caching of non-PHI content).

What I’ve done in the sheet:
- Column A: request type (chat/generation/embeddings)
- Column B: avg tokens in/out (we used HealthForge sample payloads)
- Column C: expected batching factor (default 1.6; shows sensitivity to 1.2 / 2.4)
- Column D: KV cache hit rate (default 18%; scenario table at 5/18/40%)
- Column E: per-token unit cost and blended tokens/$ estimate

If we get the two data points above (endpoint profile + QPS), I’ll lock the final numbers and send a one-pager ready for procurement.

Thanks — aiming to keep this tight for the expedited close.

Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Expedited close — cost crosswalk and batching/caching assumptions

Olga —

Thanks for the quick turn. A few clarifying Qs from our end before we align procurement: 

1) Endpoint profile: we expect to need the low-latency profile for our clinician-facing flows (about 35% of calls) and standard for background summarization. Can you confirm how you blended latency vs unit cost in the sheet?

2) QPS: steady-state is roughly 120 qps, but we expect a P95 burst to ~520 qps during morning sync windows. Is the model scalable (autoscale) or do we need a Dedicated pool commitment to hit your assumed batching?

3) Caching: our legal team flagged that some prompts may include PHI. We need recommendations for a cache policy that avoids storing PHI tokens; can you share gating checks?

Also — procurement wanted a single-line summary we can paste into the SOW that shows tokens/$ at three traffic tiers (pilot / steady / scale). Can you provide that?

Samuel Turner
Head of Platform Engineering, HealthForge
samuel.turner@healthforge.com

Olga — forwarding Samuel's questions. Quick notes for a reply draft: 

- Latency blending: we modeled low-latency as a per-token multiplier (~1.6x cost vs standard) and an assumed lower batching factor (1.2) for low-latency flows. For standard we used batching 2.0 baseline. Will call out the exact rows in HF_MAP_Costs_v3.xlsx.
- Autoscale vs Dedicated: Redwood can autoscale for hosted customers but the MAP must include a capacity plan. For their P95 bursts, recommend a hybrid plan: Dedicated reserved baseline to cover 300 qps and hosted burst capacity for the remaining variance; show cost delta in the sheet.
- PHI & caching: Kimberly — can you give the legal-safe cache policy bullets (no storage of identified PHI tokens; use token redaction + client-side prompt hashing)?

If we answer inline and attach the single-line tokens/$ summary for the three tiers (pilot, steady, scale) they can paste into SOW. I can draft that snippet.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Solutions Engineering

Subject: Re: Expedited close — cost crosswalk and batching/caching assumptions

Samuel / Alicia —

Appreciate the detail. Below are the concrete answers and the paste-ready SOW snippet (in bold). We attached an updated HF_MAP_Costs_v3.xlsx with the blend rows highlighted.

1) Latency blending:
- Low-latency profile: modeled as 1.6x per-token cost relative to standard due to smaller batching windows and higher dedicated kernel overhead. Baseline batching = 1.2 for low-latency; baseline batching = 2.0 for standard. See sheet, tab "Blend_Rates".

2) Capacity / autoscale guidance:
- Redwood hosted autoscale will serve spikes, but to guarantee P95 SLAs and predictable unit economics we recommend: Reserved Dedicated baseline for 300 qps (committed), plus hosted burst for up to additional 300 qps. Cost impact: Dedicated baseline increases fixed monthly by ~22% vs fully-hosted but reduces blended tokens/$ by 12% at scale due to improved batching and KV locality. See sheet, tab "Capacity_Scenarios".

3) Caching & PHI gating:
- We recommend a conservative policy: do not persist raw prompts flagged by your PHI detector. Instead: client-side redaction OR prompt-hash-only caching, with an allowlist for non-PHI prompt prefixes. This is implemented as an opt-in policy in our Private deployment; for Hosted we provide a managed prefix cache with redaction hooks. Kimberly, Jordan — attaching a short checklist for procurement requirements.

SOW paste-ready snippet (you can paste below into your SOW):

"Redwood Inference pricing assumptions (pilot / steady / scale): tokens-per-dollar (blended) = 2.8k TPM/$ (pilot) / 9.4k TPM/$ (steady, mixed low-latency 35%) / 15.8k TPM/$ (scale, Dedicated baseline + bursts). Assumptions: batching factors (pilot=1.2, steady=1.9, scale=2.6), KV-cache ensemble hit rates (pilot=5%, steady=18%, scale=40%). See HF_MAP_Costs_v3.xlsx for sensitivity ranges."

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll schedule a 30-min procurement alignment tomorrow to confirm the Dedicated baseline duration and SOW wording.
- Ben will provide the line-item delta for monthly committed capacity vs fully-hosted.
- Kimberly will drop the PHI cache checklist into the shared drive.

If that all looks good I’ll update the MAP and push the one-pager for procurement.

Thanks,
Olga
